plan.value: square, 3 x 3 bays (三間五重塔婆 / 方三間)
plan.source: souda-kyoto.jp/guide/spot/houkanji.html ; kyoto-design.jp/spot/2833 (search snippets quoting the designation text '三間五重塔婆、本瓦葺')

rebuild.value: 1440 (永享12年), with support of shogun Ashikaga Yoshinori, after the 1436 fire

designation.value: Important Cultural Property (重要文化財), building

central_pillar.value: shinbashira runs from the original (Hakuho-style, tuff) foundation stone to the top of the sorin without intermediate support

interior_access.value: storeys 1-2 open to visitors irregularly; Five Wisdom Buddhas on storey 1

first_storey_side_m.note: sources disagree: '6.4 m四方' vs '四辺三間（約5.5m）'; not from an official survey

basis: NDL Collaborative Reference entry (https://crd.ndl.go.jp/reference/entry/index.php?page=ref_view&id=1000061716) lists several published heights: 塔身 36.4 m, 総高 38.8 m, ~46 m, 40 m (as summarised by web search; page not fetchable here).
PLATEAU measuredHeight 28.7 m = top-roof apex (thin sorin not captured by aerial survey) [measured].

Photo ratio sorin / (apex - first eave) = 0.51 (File:Yasaka-Dori - panoramio.jpg, telephoto from ~160 m) with PLATEAU first-eave 8.3 m and apex 28.7 m gives sorin ~10.4 m and total ~39.1 m [estimated_from_photo].

Frontal ratio top-roof eave width / tier spacing = 3.2 with measured lowest-roof outline 15.1 m and ~5 %/tier taper gives tier spacing ~3.8 m, consistent with PLATEAU's ~4.0 m stepped tiers; first-eave-to-tip = 7.4 tier spacings ~29 m -> tip ~37-38 m.

popular_figure.note: Most tourist sources and OSM height=46. Not consistent with the measured footprint/roof apex: for 46 m the sorin would have to be ~17 m (37 % of the total) or every tier ~5.1 m apart with ~19.6 m-wide lowest eaves, both contradicted by the photos and the 15.1 m roof outline. 49 m and 40 m also appear. DECISION FOR LEAD: use 38.8 for geometric consistency, or 46 if matching the popular figure matters more.

w.note: body 6.4 m + ~1.5 m margin each side; stone kidan partly visible behind the street fence

material.value: cut granite/stone kerbs, stone steps up from the precinct gate

lowest_roof_outline_m.note: OSM traced outline is 13.26 x 12.99 m (area 172 m2) - probably traced inside the eave edge; PLATEAU preferred

eave_width_taper.value: about 5 % of the lowest eave width per storey (top/lowest ~0.80)
eave_width_taper.evidence: eave widths 5th:4th:3rd = 415:440:465 px (File:Yasaka Pagoda (24922466195).jpg, frontal from W), 255:270:285 px (File:Yasaka no Tō.jpg, oblique), 175:183:190 px (File:法観寺八坂の塔 - panoramio - くろふね.jpg, oblique, near-level)

body_to_eave_ratio.evidence: 3rd-storey body ~190 px vs 3rd eave ~465 px in File:Yasaka Pagoda (24922466195).jpg; matches documented 6.4 m / measured 15.1 m

tier_spacing_m.evidence: regular eave-to-eave spacing ~61 px vs top eave width 195 px (ratio 3.2) in File:Yasaka-Dori - panoramio.jpg; PLATEAU stepped tiers 3.84-4.40 m

top_roof_rise.value: apex ~0.85-1.2 tier spacings above the 5th eave

roof_curve.value: gently concave roof planes, modest upturn at corners (soft 反り); deep eaves

sorin_height_m.note: 2.3-2.5 tier spacings (Files 'Yasaka-Dori - panoramio', 'Yasaka no Tō', 'くろふね'); 10.1 m makes apex 28.7 + sorin = 38.8

kurin_rings.note: nine rings counted on enhanced crop; 9 is also the standard count

value: suien (openwork flame panels, visible as a cage-like element)

material_colour.value: dark bronze / blackened copper alloy, matt

lightning_conductor.value: thin cable from the finial down one corner of the tiers to the ground

timber_finish.value: unpainted (no vermilion), weathered dark brown-black timber

infill_panels.value: small light (white/cream plaster) panels between bracket sets and in frieze zones

bracketing.value: multi-step projecting bracket sets carrying deep eaves (likely mitesaki 三手先)

rafters.value: two layers of closely spaced rafters (二軒繁垂木)

hip_ridges.value: tiled hip ridges ending in onigawara at each corner

wind_bells.value: futaku bells hanging at the four corners of each roof

balconies.value: railed balconies (高欄) visible above roofs on upper storeys
